newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Huge Burns Philp sale perplexes market.
newsitem.headline: Huge Burns Philp sale perplexes market.

text.p: Brokers and analysts were left perplexed on Friday by a raid on yeast and spice group Burns Philp & Co Ltd, which netted 14.7 percent of the company's shares and valued the troubled firm at A$1.33 billion.

The identity of the buyer was unknown, although broker Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, which purchased the 78.16 million shares, said its client was not an international food group and did not hold any food assets at present.
Speculation centred on an offshore private individual or a private company, although investment group Brierley Investments Ltd of New Zealand was seen as a possible purchaser.
Most analysts believed a takeover was not imminent given the uncertainty of ongoing litigation over Estage Mortgage Trusts.
Estate Mortgage, for which a Burns Philp subsidiary was trustee, collapsed in 1990 with A$600 million in losses.

Contrary to speculation in this morning's newspapers, sources close to Sir Ron Brierley said it was highly unlikely that the New Zealand businessman would be involved in the transactions. They noted that his Australian vehicle, Tyndall
Australia Ltd, was currently suing a unit of Burns Philp over the Estate Mortgage collapse.
Analysts contacted by Reuters said the buyer was most likely from overseas and interested in holding a significant stake, either in the event of a takeover or to push for asset sales.
The A$2.50 paid to build up the stake appeared a full price, although one noted Burns Philp was near the bottom of its earnings cycle.
Another analyst pointed to the quality of the group's yeast business, where it has 16 percent of the world's bakers' yeast market.
The DMG offer price was 47 cents or 23 percent above Burns' A$2.03 closing price on Thursday.
Speculation about the identity of the buyer centred on a private group, with one suggesting the share raid could be a prelude to a leveraged buyout by a wealthy private investor.

"It's pretty certain it's a private company. There would be enormous flak for a publicly-listed company trying to take it on when the Estage Mortgage litigation is undecided," said a Sydney-based analyst.
Another said the buy order was believed to have been mooted previously, but cancelled.
Any move by a foreign buyer to lift its stake beyond 14.9 percent would require approval from the Foreign Investment Review Board, analysts said.

Burns Philp last month said it would sell its herb and spice businesses to focus on yeast after failing to extract sufficient returns from its strategy to become a major player in the international herb and spice market.

In particular, the company ended up second-best in a fight for U.S. market share with spice group McCormick and Co Inc. Analysts do not believe the U.S. company would be a bidder, but in its most recent public statement said it was
evaluating several options following the divestment announcement by the Australian company.
Burns Philp shares touched A$2.51 in early trade, but settled back to A$2.40 by 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT) with about 10 million shares traded.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
